title: Community Chat Feature Implementation
summary: Implemented a native JUCE chat feature for SAMPLAR with a Python FastAPI backend on the license server. Users can now communicate in real-time using HTTP polling.

ChatService.description: Core chat service with HTTP polling (3-second interval), rate limiting (10 messages/10 seconds), JWT authentication integration, and message caching

ChatPage.description: Native JUCE chat UI with message bubbles, scrollable message list, input field, connection status indicator, and dark theme styling

chat_service_plugin.description: BIBLE.MD compliant plugin providing chat REST API endpoints, message storage, user presence tracking, and rate limiting

SAMPLAR_client.changes: Changed onGoCommunity to onGoChat, renamed communityButton_ to chatButton_
Updated button text from COMMUNITY to CHAT, updated callback references
Added ChatPage at index 8, added chat navigation callback, updated resized() to include chat bounds
Added ChatService.h/.cpp and ChatPage.h/.cpp to target_sources

GET /api/chat/history.auth: Bearer token (same JWT as license system)

architecture_decisions.http_polling_vs_websocket: HTTP polling (3-second interval) chosen for MVP simplicity. WebSocket can be added in Phase 2 for real-time.
architecture_decisions.auth_integration: Uses same JWT token and AUTH_SECRET_KEY as license system - no separate login required.
architecture_decisions.rate_limiting: 10 messages per 10 seconds per user, enforced both client-side and server-side.
architecture_decisions.page_index: ChatPage added at index 8 to preserve CommunityPage at index 7 for backwards compatibility.

fixes_applied.issue: ChatPollTimer could not access private pollMessages() method
fixes_applied.solution: Added 'friend class ChatPollTimer' declaration in ChatService.h
